text:
## Desktop capability map

**Scope:** A local Windows desktop app should use lunR's existing runtime, not emulate its TUI or reimplement agent behavior. `REMOTE_DESKTOP_HANDOFF.md` places the desktop app after TUI work and the separately downloaded remote host after desktop work. The remote-device gateway is therefore a placeholder in this plan. The existing Telegram/Discord gateway stays.

| Built-in capability and source | Graphical adaptation |
| --- | --- |
| Providers, OAuth, catalog and model selection: `src/core/model-runtime.ts`, `src/core/auth-storage.ts`, `src/core/grok-cli-auth.ts`, `src/core/subscriptions.ts`, `src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts` at the login, model and refresh handlers; `src/builtin-extensions/lunr-local-providers/index.ts`, `pi-ollama-cloud/index.ts` | Provide credential setup, OAuth prompts/callback feedback, login/logout, stored-credential model picker, refresh status and local-provider discovery. Preserve xAI Grok CLI import behavior. Model tiers and per-tier thinking come from `src/core/model-tiers.ts`. Thinking controls come from `src/builtin-extensions/ashxj-thinking.ts`; Codex-only persistent Fast mode comes from `src/core/settings-manager.ts` and the interactive Fast handler. Do not present Fast as a paid OpenAI API option. |
| Permission modes, plan and goal: `src/core/permissions.ts`, `permission-mode.ts`, `permission-mode-control.ts`, `src/builtin-extensions/lunr-plan-tools.ts`, `narumiruna-pi-goal/src/goal.ts` | Show the active manual/yolo/plan/auto mode and a real approval UI for tools, large child launches and `present_plan`, including rejection feedback. Show goal state and its forced Auto transition. Preserve fail-closed mutating-tool behavior when an approval channel is absent. |
| Subagents and intercom: `src/builtin-extensions/pi-subagents/src/extension/index.ts`, `intercom/native-supervisor-channel.ts`, `slash/slash-commands.ts`, `tui/render.ts`, `src/core/subagent-cancellation.ts`, `src/builtin-extensions/pi-intercom/index.ts` | Show individual children, selected tier or explicit model, progress, results, failures and recovery controls. Support async-by-default launches, foreground preview, wait, stop, resume, indexed steering and correlated parent/child questions. Address children by private `childId`, not display descriptions. Distinguish an answered question from a delivery receipt or final result; cancellation must not wake a stopped parent. Intercom's built-in TUI compose/session views need graphical equivalents if exposed. |
| Cron and bot gateway: `src/core/cron/{jobs,scheduler,origin-context}.ts`, `src/builtin-extensions/lunr-cron.ts`, `src/gateway/{cron,router,approval,authz}.ts`, `src/gateway/adapters/{telegram,discord}.ts` | Give jobs a schedule, destination, history and run/pause/resume/remove controls. **Decide scheduler ownership explicitly:** TUI cron starts only for `ctx.mode === "tui"` and runs in that live session; the bot gateway runs the shared scheduler with fresh headless sessions and delivers to chat platforms. Starting a second desktop scheduler against the same jobs without ownership rules risks duplicate fires. Keep bot pairing, authorization, approvals and delivery intact; do not relabel it the future remote-device gateway. |
| Coding, web, LSP and MCP tools: `src/core/tools/`, `src/builtin-extensions/pi-web-access/index.ts`, `pi-lsp-extension/src/index.ts`, `pi-mcp-adapter/index.ts` | Render tool arguments, streaming output, errors, diffs and expandable results graphically. Supply graphical web-search curator review, LSP status/configuration and MCP setup, OAuth, consent, elicitation and hosted MCP UI interaction. Web search currently opens a separate interactive curator; MCP UI can open Glimpse or a browser (`pi-mcp-adapter/ui-session.ts`). These are **built-in interactions**, not a commitment to render arbitrary third-party extension components. I found no registered first-party `browser` automation tool in `src/builtin-extensions/index.ts` or `src/core/tools/`; native computer use is recorded as unfinished in `AGENTS.md`. If "browser" means an agent-controlled page rather than curator/MCP interaction, that is a separate capability decision, not existing parity. |
| Skills, commands, instructions and memory: `src/core/{skills,prompt-templates,resource-loader,slash-commands,settings-manager}.ts`, `src/builtin-extensions/{simple-pi-memory,lunr-skill-creator/index,pi-prompt-template-model/index}.ts` | Offer graphical skill discovery/invocation and tag completion, prompt templates, built-in commands, context/reload status, settings and memory controls. Keep `/skill:name` expansion distinct from a skill tag, which inserts a mention. Memory enablement controls injection and tools without deleting facts. Preserve trust gating for project resources and the user-managed global/model instruction files. |
| Sessions and file recovery: `src/core/rollback.ts`, `src/core/agent-session-runtime.ts`, `src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts` at undo/edit/redo/rollback handlers | Provide session browsing, tree navigation, fork/clone, compaction and export. Undo/edit/redo navigate the **same session**; edit restores the message and image chips to the composer. Rollback restores file snapshots and **forks**. Show its file-impact confirmation distinctly from conversational rewind. |
| Tool/thinking presentation, activity, todos and usage: `src/modes/interactive/components/{tool-execution,assistant-message,usage-view}.ts`, `src/modes/interactive/smooth-streaming.ts`, `src/builtin-extensions/{ashxj-tui,ashxj-spinners,pi-tps,lunr-todos}.ts`, `src/core/{subagent-spinner,usage-service,customize}.ts` | Use structured message/tool events for expandable cards, hidden/collapsed thinking, smooth reveal if desired, child activity, todo lists, token/context/cache/TPS and subscription-plan usage. Preserve the distinction between current-session usage and provider plan usage. Graphical animation need not reproduce terminal glyphs, but the selected spinner setting and child status must remain intelligible. Add graphical image attachment and `[image_n]` editing rather than terminal clipboard shortcuts. |

All paths in the table are relative to `packages/coding-agent/`.

### Integration findings

- **Blocker: RPC is not desktop feature parity.** `src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts` exposes prompts, steering, model/thinking changes, session/tree data and basic extension dialogs. Its `get_state` has no permission-mode, goal, cron or subagent state; `get_commands` excludes built-in TUI commands; `src/core/slash-commands.ts` and `src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts` own many of those actions. `docs/rpc.md` explicitly says built-in TUI commands cannot be invoked through RPC `prompt`. `rpc-mode.ts` also makes `custom()` unavailable, ignores component widgets and custom footer/editor, and does not support autocomplete composition. A desktop protocol needs typed actions, state snapshots and events for the built-ins rather than command-string or terminal-output parsing.
- **High: approval ownership needs design before implementation.** `src/core/permissions.ts` registers an approval handler and treats `present_plan` specially: with no handler it reports that the user will review later, while mutating tool gates fail closed. Desktop process/view disconnects must have an explicit pending-approval policy. The graphical client must not silently turn an absent approval UI into consent.
- **High: runtime lifetime is not view lifetime.** `src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts` disposes its runtime on shutdown. Reopening a saved JSONL session restores history, not an in-flight tool, approval dialog or child. The local desktop process boundary needs ownership and reconnect behavior; the later remote host must reuse that runtime rather than fork it.
- **Medium: TUI-specific bridges need structured replacements.** `src/builtin-extensions/index.ts` distinguishes light and deferred features; `ashxj-tui.ts` owns footer customization, `lunr-cron.ts` checks `"tui"` before starting its scheduler, and subagent/intercom/MCP interfaces include `ctx.ui.custom()` components. Audit each built-in's interaction and lifecycle as it moves to graphical mode. Do not promise graphical support for third-party custom TUI components; the requested scope is built-ins.
- **Medium: clarify browser scope.** `pi-web-access/index.ts` supports an interactive browser curator and `pi-mcp-adapter/ui-session.ts` supports browser-hosted MCP UI. Neither establishes first-party browser automation or native computer use. Treat those as separate product requirements if intended.

**Focused validation for the eventual implementation:** Add contract tests for typed desktop state/actions against the same runtime as the CLI; approval timeout/disconnect and plan feedback; single-owner cron firing while desktop and bot gateway coexist; subagent question/answer/stop/reconnect ordering; OAuth and MCP elicitation through the graphical dialog channel; session undo versus file rollback; and graphical rendering of streamed tools, thinking, images, todos and usage. Existing useful baselines include `test/{rpc,permissions,plan-approval,gateway-cron,supervisor-question-lifecycle,subagent-escape,interactive-mode-undo-edit,rollback,agent-memory,usage-view}.test.ts`. **No tests were run** for this read-only mapping.

The product choices worth settling are whether desktop owns a persistent local runtime after its window closes, how it arbitrates cron ownership with a running bot gateway, and whether "browser" requires agent-controlled browsing beyond the existing curator and MCP interfaces. Remote-device gateway packaging and pairing can wait for its later milestone.

### Integration findings

- **Blocker: RPC is not desktop feature parity.** `src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts` exposes prompts, steering, model/thinking changes, session/tree data and basic extension dialogs. Its `get_state` has no permission-mode, goal, cron or subagent state; `get_commands` excludes built-in TUI commands; `src/core/slash-commands.ts` and `src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts` own many of those actions. `docs/rpc.md` explicitly says built-in TUI commands cannot be invoked through RPC `prompt`. `rpc-mode.ts` also makes `custom()` unavailable, ignores component widgets and custom footer/editor, and does not support autocomplete composition. A desktop protocol needs typed actions, state snapshots and events for the built-ins rather than command-string or terminal-output parsing.
- **High: approval ownership needs design before implementation.** `src/core/permissions.ts` registers an approval handler and treats `present_plan` specially: with no handler it reports that the user will review later, while mutating tool gates fail closed. Desktop process/view disconnects must have an explicit pending-approval policy. The graphical client must not silently turn an absent approval UI into consent.
- **High: runtime lifetime is not view lifetime.** `src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts` disposes its runtime on shutdown. Reopening a saved JSONL session restores history, not an in-flight tool, approval dialog or child. The local desktop process boundary needs ownership and reconnect behavior; the later remote host must reuse that runtime rather than fork it.
- **Medium: TUI-specific bridges need structured replacements.** `src/builtin-extensions/index.ts` distinguishes light and deferred features; `ashxj-tui.ts` owns footer customization, `lunr-cron.ts` checks `"tui"` before starting its scheduler, and subagent/intercom/MCP interfaces include `ctx.ui.custom()` components. Audit each built-in's interaction and lifecycle as it moves to graphical mode. Do not promise graphical support for third-party custom TUI components; the requested scope is built-ins.
- **Medium: clarify browser scope.** `pi-web-access/index.ts` supports an interactive browser curator and `pi-mcp-adapter/ui-session.ts` supports browser-hosted MCP UI. Neither establishes first-party browser automation or native computer use. Treat those as separate product requirements if intended.

**Focused validation for the eventual implementation:** Add contract tests for typed desktop state/actions against the same runtime as the CLI; approval timeout/disconnect and plan feedback; single-owner cron firing while desktop and bot gateway coexist; subagent question/answer/stop/reconnect ordering; OAuth and MCP elicitation through the graphical dialog channel; session undo versus file rollback; and graphical rendering of streamed tools, thinking, images, todos and usage. Existing useful baselines include `test/{rpc,permissions,plan-approval,gateway-cron,supervisor-question-lifecycle,subagent-escape,interactive-mode-undo-edit,rollback,agent-memory,usage-view}.test.ts`. **No tests were run** for this read-only mapping.

The product choices worth settling are whether desktop owns a persistent local runtime after its window closes, how it arbitrates cron ownership with a running bot gateway, and whether "browser" requires agent-controlled browsing beyond the existing curator and MCP interfaces. Remote-device gateway packaging and pairing can wait for its later milestone.
